measured: Read 2026-10-07. twin-world's generated demand names Twitch for Postiz alone, and Postiz's Twitch channel is owner-excluded (below), so this pack's demand is the owner's ruling of 2026-10-07 for an AI VTuber stream rig that rehearses against the twin instead of live Twitch: "make sure to build it in the idiomatic p3 manner" and "the main focus of the twitch pack should be the UI mirror of course. And the fact that you can actually video cast to it". It is read as three callers: the rig itself (agent-stream on volter-desktop, an unversioned working copy read at the paths below), which streams through OBS to Twitch's RTMP ingest and reads its channel's chat anonymously over IRC on WebSocket; the people on twitch.tv the ruling names, the streamer at the creator dashboard and anyone at the channel page; and the simulated viewers, a program outside the World that posts chat as each viewer's own account through the API (each viewer authorizes it on id.twitch.tv, and it validates its tokens as Twitch requires). The vendor quickstart's first call (Get Started: an app access token from the client credentials grant, then Get Users) is the installed customer entry. Searches of twin-world (packages, apps, cookbook, scripts, architecture) and of the other packs found no Twitch call. EventSub, raids, follows and subscriptions are reached by none of these callers and are not served.

applications.name: agent-stream (the AI VTuber stream rig)
applications.client: Node's global WebSocket (chat.js, the streamer's read-only chat reader) and OBS Studio's custom RTMP output driven over obs-websocket (obs.js)

backend.call: CAP REQ :twitch.tv/tags, then PASS SCHMOOPIIE and NICK justinfan<5 digits>: an anonymous, read-only login
each tagged PRIVMSG parsed for its display-name, color and text
OBS's stream service set to rtmp_custom, server rtmp://live.twitch.tv/app with the channel's stream key (and ?bandwidthtest=true for a test), then StartStream and StopStream

frontend.call: the streamer copies the channel's Primary Stream key into stream-key.txt

applications.name: twitch.tv (the owner rehearsing the stream)
applications.client: twitch.tv's own web client, driven by people: the streamer signed in at the creator dashboard, viewers at the channel page and its chat

frontend.call: signing in at www.twitch.tv/login with the account's password
frontend.evidence: the owner, 2026-10-07: "the main focus of the twitch pack should be the UI mirror of course"

frontend.call: the channel page: its player playing the broadcast (or the offline view), the live chat, the viewer count, the title and the category
frontend.evidence: the owner, 2026-10-07: "the main focus of the twitch pack should be the UI mirror of course. And the fact that you can actually video cast to it"

frontend.call: chatting from the channel page or its chat popout as the person signed in
frontend.evidence: the owner, 2026-10-07: "the main focus of the twitch pack should be the UI mirror of course"

frontend.call: the stream manager: live status, viewers, Edit Stream Info's title and category, and the streamer's chat
frontend.operation: getStreams; getChannelInformation; modifyChannelInformation; searchCategories; sendChatMessage; stream-manager (screen)
frontend.evidence: the owner, 2026-10-07: "the main focus of the twitch pack should be the UI mirror of course"

applications.name: the simulated viewers (a program outside the World posting chat as its viewers' own accounts)
applications.commit: owner's ruling of 2026-10-07 (the program is written against Twitch's documented flows)
applications.client: plain HTTPS requests: the authorization code grant flow (https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/authentication/getting-tokens-oauth/), token validation (https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/authentication/validate-tokens/) and Send Chat Message (https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/api/reference/#send-chat-message)

backend.call: each viewer sent to https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&scope=user:write:chat, signing in and clicking Authorize
POST https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/token grant_type=authorization_code, and grant_type=refresh_token when a token is no longer valid
GET https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/validate when it starts and hourly after
backend.evidence: https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/authentication/validate-tokens/ (Your app must validate the OAuth token when it starts and on an hourly basis thereafter)

backend.call: GET https://api.twitch.tv/helix/users?login=<channel>, the broadcaster's id (each viewer's own id is the validate answer's user_id)
POST https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/revoke when a viewer's session ends

applications.name: the installed customer entry (Twitch's Get Started)
applications.client: plain HTTPS requests and Node's global WebSocket, with TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET from the developer console

backend.call: POST https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/token grant_type=client_credentials: an app access token
GET https://api.twitch.tv/helix/users?login=<channel> with the app access token

excluded.what: Postiz's Twitch channel provider (libraries/nestjs-libraries/src/integrations/social/twitch.provider.ts: its OAuth on id.twitch.tv and its Helix calls)
excluded.why: owner-excluded long tail: twin-world's demand/applications.json names Postiz's twitch channel so (its `ships.twitch`), so no Postiz call is demand here
